add_opinions.stance: The commoditisation pressure isn't cyclical â€” it's structural. Foundation models have a systematic incentive to absorb wrapper value because it reduces user dependency on intermediaries. Small teams adopting wrappers are implicitly betting against that incentive.

The right question for every AI tool in a small team's stack isn't 'is this useful?' but 'will this still exist as an independent product in 18 months, or will the underlying model absorb it natively?' Usefulness and durability are separate dimensions that teams conflate.

Adding new abstraction layers on top of agents (like the 'Claws' pattern) is a red flag, not a feature â€” each additional layer multiplies commoditisation surface and reduces operational defensibility for dependent teams

Teams need to evaluate tools on two axes: operational reality AND durability.
